title: Warm or cool? The two old scales, explained
caption:
'Hot-headed' gets thrown around a lot. Here's what the old idea actually meant.

In Unani tradition, which goes back to the Greek physicians, temperament runs on two scales: warm or cool, and moist or dry. Together they make four elements. The 'hot-headed' friend might be Air (loud, then over it in five minutes) or Fire (quieter, sharper, keeping score).

Traditional wellness wisdom, not medical advice.

Try the self-check on slide 5, then send this to the friend you've always called hot-headed.
